records.text: sev2 checkout-svc: paged 03:12, ack 2m later, rollback shipped in 6m flat once triggered. green light at 03:49 so page-to-resolved runs 37m. CDN vendor's ticket quoted a 4h ETA for the underlying cert issue, way off — we didn't wait on them. sev2 SLA target is 15m, blown as usual. postmortem due friday.

[9:02 AM] priya: db-primary flapped again
[9:04 AM] priya: this is the same class of failover we saw last tuesday (that one ran 25m start to finish)
[10:35 PM] priya: ok confirmed stable, replica promoted for good. started 9:03am, called it at 10:35pm — 13h32m of degraded reads.
[10:36 PM] dae: brutal. on-call rotation says 30m response SLA, we blew way past that too.

auth-svc outage. incident opened 14:02Z. root cause: expired cert on IdP. fix rolled 14:30 (28m to build+push), didn't take. second attempt landed, service healthy by 16:31Z. incident window 14:02–16:31 = 149m. vendor SSO provider's status page still showed a 6h ETA for their side, irrelevant since we self-mitigated. hold time with vendor support: 52m before we gave up and fixed it ourselves.

[11:47] omar: search is 500ing
[11:48] omar: yeah confirmed, cache node OOM'd
[11:49] omar: restarted the pod
[11:52] omar: green again, so ~5 min blip start to finish
[11:53] jules: fast turnaround, nice. compare to the queue outage two weeks back that ran 3h+, this was nothing.

batch-pipeline stuck. flagged during monday morning review of dead-letter queue growth, but going back through logs the jobs actually stopped consuming at 2026-07-28 06:14 and nobody caught it until 2026-07-31 00:15 when a downstream report came back empty. that's 3961 minutes of silent data loss before remediation started. planned maintenance the week prior was scheduled for 90m and finished on time, unrelated. the estimated backfill time once we noticed was quoted at 6h by the pipeline owner, which also proved wrong — the actual backfill ran overnight into the next day.

[3:10pm] lena: payments-gateway degraded, elevated 5xx
[3:14pm] lena: incident declared
[7:38pm] lena: fully recovered, error rate back to baseline. that's 4h28m start to finish, ouch
[7:39pm] raf: our payments SLA with the processor guarantees 99.9% which we've already blown for the month
[7:40pm] raf: also worth noting the maintenance window scheduled for tonight (11pm-1am, 2h) is now pointless since we already ate the downtime

cdn-edge sev3. began 22:04 UTC (first 5xx spike), edge fully drained/recovered 23:35 UTC — ninety-one minutes end to end. akamai support quoted a 3h turnaround for their side before we self-resolved by failing over to origin. separately, the deploy that introduced the bad cache header took 11m to roll out originally, back on tuesday.

[Mon 8:03am] theo: notifications-svc silently dropping messages
[Mon 8:05am] theo: not obvious from dashboards, only caught via customer complaint
[Tue 8:10am] theo: root caused and patched, queue draining now
[Tue 8:10am] theo: called it resolved right there, so from first drop to fix that's 24h7m, brutal
[Tue 8:15am] priya: reminds me of the SLA target for P1 which is supposed to be 4h detection max, we way overshot on detection alone

lb-frontend flap. 09:41 alert fires, 09:44 ack, mitigated via manual failover at 10:03. window 09:41-10:03 = 22m. runbook estimate for this exact playbook says 'expect ~10m', we ran over. previous incident of same class two months ago took 55m so this was an improvement.

[2:00am] dev: db replication lag alert
[2:02am] dev: paging dba on-call
[12:34pm] dba: ok replication caught up fully, closing this out. from first alert to fully caught up: 10h34m
[12:36pm] dev: yikes. our internal target for replication lag recovery is 45m, we were nowhere close
[12:37pm] dba: the vendor's replication tool support said their typical fix window is 'a few hours' when we opened the ticket at 6am, they were optimistic

long-tail sev1: image-processing queue backed up starting fri 2026-07-24 16:00, not fully drained until sun 2026-07-26 18:05. that's 3005 minutes end to end. the initial on-call estimate given to leadership friday evening was 'should clear by morning' (roughly 16h), which missed badly. weekly cron maintenance saturday 02:00-02:30 (30m) ran as scheduled and was not a factor.

[5:20pm] mia: checkout errors spiking again
[7:18pm] mia: confirmed resolved, rolled back the bad feature flag
[7:19pm] mia: 5:20 to 7:18 is basically 118 minutes of degraded checkout
[7:20pm] noah: last month's similar flag issue only lasted 15m, this one was way worse
[7:21pm] mia: also the flag rollback itself only took like 90 seconds once we found the toggle, most of the time was spent diagnosing

search-svc: 500s began 01:15, resolved 02:31 after restarting the affected shard. 76m of impact. shard restart itself: ~4m. an earlier false alarm at 00:40 (2m blip, self-recovered) is unrelated to this incident.

[10:00] carlos: email delivery delayed across the board
[14:15] carlos: queue fully drained, delivery times back to normal
[14:16] carlos: four hours and change from start to clear — call it 4h15m even
[14:17] sam: our contractual SLA with customers is 30m max delay before we owe credits, so this triggers that
[14:18] carlos: vendor SMTP relay's status page originally promised restoration 'within the hour' when we opened the case at 10:30, obviously didn't happen

slow-burn sev2: elevated latency on recommendations-svc first noted 2026-07-20 09:00, didn't cross back under threshold until 2026-07-21 16:33. 31h33m = 1893m. planned failover drill the following week is budgeted at 45m and is unrelated. initial triage guess was 'probably a few hours,' which was off by more than a day.

[4:30pm] gina: api gateway rate limiting everyone incorrectly
[5:14pm] gina: fix deployed and confirmed, rate limits back to normal
[5:15pm] gina: 44 minutes start to finish, not our worst
[5:16pm] leo: still busts the 20m internal target for gateway config issues
[5:17pm] gina: the actual config change itself was like 3 lines, took 90 seconds to write, all the rest was CI

storage-svc degradation: 2026-06-02 03:00 first alert, 2026-06-02 11:32 fully cleared. 8h32m = 512m. the storage vendor's SLA credit threshold kicks in past 4h, so we're eligible. an earlier maintenance window that weekend (sat 01:00-03:00, 2h) was completed without issue and isn't part of this.

[9:15] wren: dns resolution failing for internal services
[9:44] wren: fixed, was a stale record, propagated and confirmed working
[9:45] wren: 29 min, could've been worse given dns caching
[9:46] priya: the ttl on that record is set to 300s (5m) which is why it cleared fast once we fixed it
[9:47] wren: yeah propagation itself was maybe 6m of that 29

data-pipeline corruption: bad rows first written 2026-05-10 14:00, discovered and fully remediated 2026-05-12 02:41. window: 2201m. customer-facing dashboards showed stale/wrong numbers this whole time. an unrelated third-party API outage the prior week ran about 3h and had already been closed out.

[1:00pm] finn: video transcoding backlog growing fast
[3:47pm] finn: backlog cleared, workers scaled back down
[3:48pm] finn: 1:00 to 3:47, that's 167 minutes of delayed uploads
[3:49pm] adaeze: the autoscaler's own target recovery time is documented as 60m, missed that by a mile
[3:50pm] finn: separately I was on hold with the cloud provider for 40m trying to get quota raised before I found a workaround that didn't need it

cache-layer sev3: 06:02 spike in latency, 07:30 back to baseline after flushing poisoned keys. 88m impact. flush operation itself took under a minute. an earlier attempt at 06:20 to restart individual nodes (took 12m) didn't help and was abandoned.

[Wed 6:00am] otis: legacy-reports-svc totally dark, nobody's getting scheduled reports
[Fri 1:40pm] otis: finally tracked it to a cron user account that got disabled during an access audit, re-enabled and reports are flowing again
[Fri 1:41pm] otis: from wed 6am to fri 1:40pm is 3340 minutes, longest outage I've personally handled
[Fri 1:42pm] priya: the access audit itself only took 20m to run originally, nobody flagged this as a side effect until now

push-notif-svc: delivery failures 12:10-13:03, 53m. root cause: expired apns cert, rotated in 4m once identified, most of the window was detection lag. an unrelated cert rotation for a different service is scheduled monthly and took its usual 15m last week.

[8:00am] sana: internal wiki completely down, 502s everywhere
[2:41pm] sana: finally back, turned out to be a disk full on the app server
[2:42pm] sana: 8am to 2:41pm, 6h41m, embarrassing given how low-stakes this service is
[2:43pm] deshawn: our internal tools have no formal SLA but the informal expectation floating around the team was 'fixed same morning', which is 4h-ish, we blew that

webhook-dispatcher: 500s 15:44-16:03, 19m. cause: bad deploy, rolled back in 3m once flagged by on-call. the deploy itself had taken 22m to build and ship originally on tuesday, unrelated timing coincidence.

[11:00pm] yara: elasticsearch cluster yellow, some shards unassigned
[11:05am] yara: cluster green again, all shards reallocated
[11:06am] yara: 11pm to 11:05am, that's 12h5m of degraded search relevance
[11:07am] milo: the runbook for shard reallocation estimates 2h for a cluster our size, we were way past that
[11:08am] yara: also fielded a call from the infra vendor who quoted 'could be up to a day' early on, glad it wasn't

identity-svc: token validation failures began 2026-04-03 05:00, cleared 2026-04-03 22:09 after cert chain fix. 17h9m = 1029m. weekly cert rotation job normally completes in 8m and had run fine the week before this, ruling it out early cost us time. downstream SLA for auth availability is 99.95%, this incident alone blows the monthly budget.

[7:30] ravi: order-svc timing out for a subset of users
[8:32] ravi: fixed, was a connection pool exhaustion, bumped the limit
[8:33] ravi: 7:30 to 8:32, 62 minutes
[8:34] beth: pool limit change itself deployed in like 90 seconds once approved, the wait was on approval which took 25m

billing-svc: invoice generation stalled 2026-03-11 09:12-13:05, 233m. stuck job queue, cleared by manual requeue (2m operation). the vendor's payment processor had an unrelated outage the same week that ran 90m and had nothing to do with our invoicing pipeline.

[2:41pm] jo: heads up, staging is down
[2:44pm] jo: oh wait this is prod not staging
[2:47pm] jo: fixed, bad env var, prod's back
[2:48pm] han: so what, like 6 minutes from first report to fix? not bad
[2:49pm] jo: yeah, compare to the staging outage last week that sat broken for 3 days because nobody cared, this got fixed way faster since it was prod

archive-svc: backup jobs silently failing starting 2026-02-14 03:00, only caught 2026-02-16 17:58 during unrelated audit. 3778m of unbacked-up data. the audit itself took 45m to run. scheduled quarterly DR test the following month is unaffected, separate system.

[10:10am] noor: payment retries failing at 3x normal rate
[12:35pm] noor: fixed, retry backoff config was misapplied in last night's deploy
[12:36pm] noor: 10:10 to 12:35, 145 minutes
[12:37pm] deja: last night's deploy itself only took 8m to roll out, the bug just didn't show until traffic picked up this morning

vpn-gateway: remote access down 07:03-08:40, 97m. certificate expired overnight, renewed manually. auto-renewal job is supposed to run 30 days before expiry and clearly didn't fire — that's a followup item, not part of this incident's clock.

[1:00am] tobi: replicaset in read-only mode, writes failing
[11:10am] tobi: primary promoted successfully, writes restored
[11:11am] tobi: 1am to 11:10am is 10h10m, one of the longer ones this quarter
[11:12am] flora: the DBA team's internal target for primary promotion is 20m under normal conditions, this was anything but normal given the split-brain we hit first

content-cdn: stale content served starting 2026-01-08 12:00, purge finally effective 2026-01-10 10:29. 2789m. purge command itself executes in under a minute once run correctly — we ran it wrong twice before getting the right cache tag. earlier that week an unrelated 20m blip from an upstream origin server had already been resolved and logged separately.

[4:00pm] petra: sms verification codes not sending
[4:33pm] petra: resolved, carrier api key had rotated and we hadn't updated it
[4:34pm] petra: 33 min end to end
[4:35pm] ilya: twilio's own status page showed no incident on their side the whole time, this was 100% on us

metrics-pipeline: dashboards showing no fresh data from 2026-09-01 00:00 through 2026-09-01 08:01. 481m. root cause: disk quota hit on the ingest node. cleanup script freed space in 90s once triggered manually; the bulk of the window was spent figuring out which node was the culprit across a dozen candidates.

[9:00] col: load balancer health checks flapping again
[9:14] col: stabilized, was a flaky health check threshold, tightened it
[9:15] col: only 14m impact, most requests probably didn't even notice
[9:16] dara: the threshold change deploy took 6m of that 14, rest was investigation

cron-orchestrator: scheduled jobs silently not firing from 2026-10-01 05:00 to 2026-10-02 00:15. 1155m. orchestrator's leader election got stuck; forcing a new election took under a minute once diagnosed. the platform's documented uptime target is 99.9% monthly, this single incident already threatens that budget.

[6:15pm] uche: graphql gateway returning partial errors
[7:23pm] uche: root caused to a downstream timeout, bumped it, errors stopped
[7:24pm] uche: 6:15 to 7:23, 68 minutes
[7:25pm] wei: the timeout bump itself was a one-line config change, merged and deployed in 5m, rest was chasing the actual downstream service

legacy-invoicing: nightly reconciliation job broken starting 2026-11-03 02:00, not fixed until 2026-11-05 12:22. 3502m of unreconciled invoices piling up. the vendor accounting system we integrate with quoted a possible root cause on their end within 2h of us opening a ticket, but that lead was a dead end and cost us more time than it saved.

[12:00pm] simi: analytics ingestion pipeline backed up hard
[3:19pm] simi: drained fully, scaled up consumers temporarily
[3:20pm] simi: 12 to 3:19, that's 199 minutes
[3:21pm] arash: our SLA doc says analytics can lag up to 60m before we consider it degraded, so most of this counted against us officially

chat-svc: websocket disconnects spiking 20:11-20:38, 27m. load balancer sticky-session config was wrong after a routine node swap; reverted in under 2m once found. node swap itself was part of a maintenance task budgeted at 15m and finished on schedule — this incident was a side effect discovered afterward.

[5:00am] bianca: fulfillment-svc stuck, no orders shipping
[7:22pm] bianca: finally cleared, stuck message in the queue was poison-pilling the consumer, purged it
[7:23pm] bianca: 5am to 7:22pm, 14h22m, worst one this year for us
[7:24pm] tunde: support said hold times with the shipping carrier's api team were like 35m each of the three times we called, that ate a chunk of our afternoon but wasn't the actual fix

feature-flag-svc: flags failing to evaluate, defaulting everyone to off, 08:50-09:31, 41m. root cause: config cache poisoned by a bad publish. cache bust takes ~30s once triggered; most of the window was identifying which of six recent flag changes caused it.

[Sat 9:00am] kwame: object storage returning 403s intermittently for a subset of buckets
[Sun 12:50pm] kwame: finally fixed, was an IAM policy change that hadn't fully propagated, forced a refresh
[Sun 12:51pm] kwame: sat 9am to sun 12:50pm, 1670 minutes give or take
[Sun 12:52pm] rosa: the IAM change itself was reviewed and approved in 15m on friday, nobody expected propagation to be the problem

search-indexer: reindex job hung, stale results served 03:30-05:23, 113m. killed and restarted the job manually (kill+restart: 90s). a scheduled full reindex is normally scoped at 4h and runs weekly without issue — this was an unscheduled hang mid-cycle, not that job.

[Thu 4:00pm] farid: internal admin panel completely inaccessible, cert error
[Sat 6:59pm] farid: cert reissued and deployed, panel's back
[Sat 7:00pm] farid: thu 4pm to sat 6:59pm is 3059 minutes, nobody noticed for way too long since it's low traffic
[Sat 7:01pm] noa: the CA's own issuance SLA is 10m for automated requests, ours took forever because the automation itself was broken, that's the real story here

rate-limiter: false-positive blocks on legit traffic, 13:00-13:58, 58m. bad regex in the block rule, patched and deployed in 3m once isolated. the regex had been sitting unreviewed in a PR for 2 weeks before merge, unrelated to incident duration itself.

[9:30am] dev: dashboard-svc timing out for enterprise tier customers
[1:14pm] dev: resolved, database index rebuild finished, queries fast again
[1:15pm] dev: 9:30 to 1:14, 3h44m, so 224 minutes
[1:16pm] pat: enterprise SLA guarantees 99.95% uptime monthly, this alone eats most of the allowed budget for the quarter
